blog_summary: The blog post highlights a concerning study from NDSS'19 that demonstrates the alarming effectiveness of voice impersonation attacks using modern speech synthesis technology. The paper reveals that humans cannot reliably distinguish between real and morphed voices, even at a biological level—brain activity (measured via fNIRS) shows no statistically significant differences when listening to original versus synthesized voices. This poses a severe security risk, as voice-based authentication and social engineering attacks become increasingly viable. The authors also note that machine learning classifiers trained on brain activity data fail to distinguish between real and morphed voices, suggesting the problem is deeply rooted in human biology. The study underscores the urgent need for machine-assisted defenses against voice impersonation, especially as synthesis technologies improve.
paper_title: The Crux of Voice (In)security: A Brain Study of Speaker Legitimacy Detection
